name: Bottled Water
descriptions: A 500ml resealable plastic bottle of plain drinking water.
Clean, neutral taste — the most basic thirst-quencher.
effects: You feel refreshed as cool water soothes a dry throat.
No strong flavor, just clean hydration.

name: Sparkling Water
descriptions: A 330ml can of carbonated water with a crisp, bubbly mouthfeel.
No sugar or flavoring — fizzy and light.
effects: Bubbles tingle on your tongue and the drink feels refreshing.
Lighter than still water but still hydrating.

name: Cola
descriptions: A 330ml can of sweet, carbonated cola with caffeine.
Sugary, fizzy, and brightly flavored — a quick pick-me-up.
effects: The sweet fizz gives a quick sugar rush and a pleasant fizz.
Tastes indulgent but is less hydrating than plain water.

name: Orange Juice
descriptions: A 250ml single-serving carton of orange juice, lightly pulpy.
Bright citrus flavor with natural sugars and vitamin C.
effects: The citrus tang feels revitalizing and pleasantly sweet.
Good for a quick boost of flavor and calories.

name: Black Coffee
descriptions: A 200ml hot cup of strong black coffee, no milk or sugar.
Bitter, aromatic and brewed for a clear caffeine lift.
effects: A sharp jolt of alertness and warmth spreads through you.
Aromatic bitterness clears the head and wakes you up.

name: Iced Tea
descriptions: A 500ml chilled bottled iced tea, lightly sweetened and brewed.
Cool and mildly caffeinated, good on a warm day.
effects: Cold, mellow tea flavor calms thirst and offers a gentle lift.
Sweetness makes it satisfyingly refreshing.

name: Milk (250ml carton)
descriptions: A 250ml carton of pasteurized cow's milk — slightly sweet and creamy.
Good source of calories and a comforting simple drink.
effects: Creamy and filling, it settles comfortably in your stomach.
Feels nourishing and mildly satisfying.

name: Hot Chocolate
descriptions: A 300ml cup of warm hot chocolate made with cocoa and milk.
Sweet, chocolatey, and comforting — often served with a frothy top.
effects: Warm sweetness soothes and comforts, offering a gentle mood lift.
The chocolatey flavor is filling and satisfying.

name: Fresh-squeezed Orange Juice (300ml)
descriptions: Cold, freshly pressed orange juice with visible pulp and bright citrus aroma.
Kept refrigerated; no added preservatives or sugar.
Served in a recyclable glass bottle — best consumed within a few days of pressing.
effects: A bright citrus burst that wakes up the senses; the pulp gives a pleasantly textured mouthfeel.
Feels very refreshing and hydrating; a light, natural sweetness without processed aftertaste.

name: Pasteurized Orange Juice Carton (1L)
descriptions: Store-bought, pasteurized orange juice in a sealed carton; smooth, slightly sweeter than fresh.
Longer shelf life unopened; refrigerate after opening.
Filtered of most pulp for a consistent texture.
effects: A smooth, sweet citrus flavor that's easy to drink in larger quantities.
Comforting and filling for a quick energy boost; less of the fresh tang of squeezed juice.

name: Cold-pressed Green Juice
descriptions: A blend of kale, spinach, cucumber, celery and a touch of apple for balance.
Cold-pressed to retain raw nutrients; kept refrigerated.
Earthy and vegetal with a slightly bitter finish.
effects: An earthy, slightly bitter sip that tastes nutrient-dense and refreshing.
Provides a clean, green lift rather than a sugary rush; might leave a mild vegetal aftertaste.

name: Shelf-stable Apple Juice Carton (200ml)
descriptions: Small, sealed carton of apple juice processed and shelf-stable until opened.
Clear, sweet apple flavor with a smooth mouthfeel.
Convenient single-serving size for travel or lunchboxes.
effects: Sweet and familiar apple flavor that's easy to sip and satisfying.
Quickly replenishes a small thirst and gives a gentle sugar lift.

name: Mixed Fruit Juice Box (apple, grape, strawberry)
descriptions: Juice box blending apple, grape and a hint of strawberry; kid-friendly and portable.
Tetra pack with a small straw attached.
Moderately sweet with a mild tartness from the berry.
effects: A small, sweet and slightly tangy drink that feels light and convenient.
Easy to drink quickly; pleasant for a short energy pick-me-up.

name: Frozen Orange Concentrate (375ml can)
descriptions: Thick orange syrup intended to be diluted with water to make multiple servings.
Very sweet and viscous when undiluted; sticky and dense.
Stored frozen for long shelf life; follow dilution instructions on the label.
effects: When diluted, produces multiple glasses of sweet orange juice with a classic flavor.
If drunk undiluted, it's overwhelmingly sweet and syrupy — satisfying as a sugar hit but not very refreshing.

name: bottled cold brew coffee
descriptions: 330 ml ready-to-drink cold brew in a dark glass bottle; smooth, concentrated coffee with chocolate and caramel notes.
Chilled and unsweetened for a clean bitter finish; designed as a quick strong pick-me-up.
effects: You drink the cold, concentrated coffee; its bold bitterness and cool body hit immediately, leaving a lingering roasted aftertaste.
The high caffeine content sharpens your focus and shakes off grogginess, giving a brisk mental clarity.

name: canned iced latte
descriptions: 330 ml canned iced latte with milk and a double-shot espresso; lightly sweetened and creamy.
Smooth, milky texture with mild coffee bitterness — a comforting ready-to-drink coffee beverage.
effects: You sip the sweet, creamy latte; the milk softens espresso's edge and leaves a warm, filling mouthfeel.
The coffee provides a steady wakefulness without the sharp jolt of straight black coffee.

name: bottled green tea
descriptions: 500 ml bottled unsweetened green tea; grassy, slightly astringent, served chilled.
Light and refreshing, made from steamed green tea leaves with a clean finish.
effects: You drink the light, grassy tea; its subtle astringency clears your palate and feels refreshingly clean.
A mild caffeine lift eases mental fog without jitteriness.

name: bottled chamomile tea
descriptions: 330 ml ready-to-drink chamomile infusion; caffeine-free with warm floral notes.
A gentle, soothing herbal tea intended for relaxation and a calm pause.
effects: You drink the floral chamomile; its soft honeyed notes and warm mouthfeel create an immediate sense of calm.
The caffeine-free infusion soothes and helps unwind after a busy day.

name: ready-to-drink matcha latte
descriptions: 250 ml canned matcha latte: finely ground Japanese green tea blended with milk for a creamy, umami-rich drink.
Vivid green color, vegetal and slightly sweet, offers a sustained, focused alertness.
effects: You drink the creamy matcha; vegetal, slightly grassy flavors and a smooth dairy body leave a satisfying richness.
Matcha delivers a calm, sustained energy that feels steadier than a sharp espresso spike.

name: sparkling cold brew coffee
descriptions: 330 ml carbonated cold brew in a can; fizzy take on cold coffee with bright, effervescent mouthfeel.
Crisp carbonation accentuates the coffee's aromatics and makes the beverage feel particularly refreshing.
effects: You drink the fizzy coffee; bubbles lift the roasted aroma and the cold sip hits with an immediate, lively jolt.
The combination of carbonation and caffeine provides an energetic, refreshing kick.

name: Whole Roasted Coffee Beans
descriptions: Dark, oil-sheened roasted coffee beans packaged for brewing or snacking.
Aromatic and crunchy; used for grinding, espresso, or nibbling a few as a quick caffeine bite.
effects: You chew a whole roasted coffee bean: a sharp, bitter hit of roastiness and acidity floods your mouth, followed by a fast, jittery lift of alertness.
The crunchy bean leaves a lingering bitter aftertaste and a slightly dry sensation on your tongue.

name: Ground Coffee (Medium Roast)
descriptions: Pre-ground medium roast coffee suitable for drip brewing.
Finer texture than whole beans; aromatic and convenient for quick preparation.
effects: You spoon a mouthful of dry ground coffee into your mouth: an immediate abrasive bitterness and strong roasted aroma overwhelm the palate.
A caffeinated buzz builds quickly, leaving a metallic dryness and a lingering bitter film.

name: Instant Coffee Granules
descriptions: Freeze-dried coffee granules that dissolve quickly into hot water for instant coffee.
Convenient and concentrated — can be eaten dry in a pinch, though intensely bitter.
effects: You pour a spoonful of instant granules into your mouth; they dissolve with an acrid, concentrated bitterness and leave a powdery dryness.
A quick, sharp caffeine spike follows, making your hands tingle with alertness.

name: Espresso Roast Beans
descriptions: Dark-roasted beans selected for high-intensity espresso shots.
Very bold, smoky flavor with a potent caffeine profile when consumed directly or brewed strong.
effects: You bite into an espresso bean: a powerful, smoky bitterness and a blast of concentrated caffeine hit your system almost immediately.
Your heart races and focus sharpens rapidly; the bean leaves a persistent roasted aftertaste.

name: Decaffeinated Coffee Beans
descriptions: Roasted beans processed to remove most caffeine while retaining coffee flavor.
Good for brewing low-caffeine coffee; nibbling yields flavor with little stimulant effect.
effects: You chew a decaf coffee bean: familiar roasted bitterness arrives, but the usual jittery lift is muted.
It tastes like coffee with the stimulation largely dialed down, leaving behind a dry, roasted mouthfeel.

name: Green Coffee Beans (Unroasted)
descriptions: Raw, unroasted coffee beans with a vegetal green aroma used for specialty preparations.
Tougher and more astringent than roasted beans; edible but intensely bitter and chewy.
effects: You bite a raw green coffee bean: a grassy, astringent flavor with astringency and a tough chew sends a sour edge to your mouth.
You feel a modest stimulant effect and an uncomfortable dryness as tannins cling to your tongue.

name: Black Tea Leaves
descriptions: Oxidized black tea leaves with robust, malty flavor notes, packaged loose.
Classic breakfast and afternoon tea base; can be steeped or chewed directly for a bitter, tannic bite.
effects: You chew a pinch of black tea leaves: strong tannic bitterness, a dry, puckering mouthfeel, and a mild caffeine lift set in.
The flavor is brisk and slightly astringent, leaving your throat dry but your mind more alert.

name: Earl Grey Loose Tea (Bergamot-Flavored)
descriptions: Black tea blended with bergamot oil for a citrus-floral aroma and slightly perfumed taste.
Commonly brewed; the dry leaves are fragrant and bitter if eaten directly.
effects: You taste a pinch of Earl Grey leaves: immediate bergamot citrus atop strong black tea bitterness, astringent and fragrant.
A light caffeine lift occurs along with a lingering citrus perfume in your mouth.

name: Green Tea Leaves (Sencha)
descriptions: Delicate steamed green tea leaves with grassy, vegetal notes and moderate caffeine.
Often brewed lightly; eaten as raw leaves they taste fresh, vegetal, and slightly bitter.
effects: You chew a mouthful of sencha leaves: fresh green, slightly grassy flavors with a pleasant but subtle bitterness.
A gentle, clear caffeine lift follows, with a mild drying sensation from the leaves' tannins.

name: Matcha Powder
descriptions: Finely ground powdered green tea used for whisked preparations and cooking.
Bright green and concentrated — ingesting raw powder is intensely vegetal and bright with caffeine and L-theanine effects.
effects: You swallow a spoonful of vivid matcha powder: a punch of grassy bitterness, followed by a focused, calm alertness rather than jagged jitters.
The powder leaves a chalky texture on your tongue and a pleasantly lingering umami note.

name: Chamomile Herbal Tea Blend
descriptions: Dried chamomile flowers blended as a caffeine-free herbal tisane, known for its calming aroma.
Caffeine-free; eating the dried flowers yields a floral, slightly sweet, calming sensation rather than stimulation.
effects: You chew a mouthful of chamomile flowers: a gentle floral sweetness and mellow apple-like notes soothe the palate.
Rather than stimulating, the herb brings a slight drowsy calm and a soft relaxation spreading through your limbs.

name: Rooibos (Red Bush) Tea Leaves
descriptions: Naturally caffeine-free South African red bush tea with sweet, woody flavors.
Used as a caffeine-free alternative; eaten raw it tastes sweet and slightly earthy rather than bitter.
effects: You chew a pinch of rooibos: a warm, naturally sweet, slightly nutty flavor with minimal astringency.
Its calming, caffeine-free profile leaves you relaxed and without the dryness typical of oxidized teas.

name: Cold-Pressed Orange Juice (Fresh)
descriptions: Freshly pressed from ripe oranges; slightly cloudy with pulp and bright citrus aroma.
Kept chilled to preserve the tart-sweet tang and natural vitamin bite.
effects: You drink the cold, pulpy orange juice — the bright citrus zing wakes your senses and leaves a clean, slightly tart finish.
The pulp gives little chewy bits between sips, making it feel unusually fresh and lively.

name: Pasteurized Apple Juice (Bottled)
descriptions: Clear golden apple juice, lightly sweet and smooth; shelf-stable until opened.
Filtered and pasteurized for a familiar, mellow flavor.
effects: You sip the smooth sweet apple nectar; it tastes comforting and simple, like taking a calm, familiar breath.
The liquid slides easily, leaving a gentle sweetness that lingers on the tongue.

name: Green Detox Juice (Kale & Cucumber)
descriptions: A deep green blend of kale, spinach, celery and cucumber; vegetal, slightly bitter and grassy.
Cold-pressed to retain enzymes and a vivid green color.
effects: You take a long pull of the green juice — the grassy kale and cool cucumber leave a fresh, slightly astringent mouthfeel.
It tastes cleansing and green, like a concentrated garden in a bottle.

name: Beet & Carrot Juice Blend
descriptions: Vibrant magenta juice with sweet earthiness from beets and bright sweetness from carrots.
Balanced between earthy and sweet, slightly thicker than plain fruit juice.
effects: You drink the beet-carrot blend and feel a sweet, earthy rush — it tastes dense and vegetal with a lingering rooty sweetness.
Its color stains the tongue, and each sip feels hearty and grounding.

name: Tropical Smoothie (Mango-Pineapple-Banana)
descriptions: Thick, creamy smoothie blending ripe mango, pineapple and banana; fibrous and rich.
More filling than juice — served cold, almost dessert-like in sweetness and texture.
effects: You drink the thick tropical smoothie; it coats your mouth with sweet, pulpy fruit and feels satisfyingly heavy.
The banana adds creaminess while mango and pineapple punch up the sweetness and tang.

name: Citrus Concentrate Syrup (Straight)
descriptions: Highly concentrated citrus syrup intended for dilution — intensely sweet and acidic in its current state.
Sticky and viscous, with an overpowering orange-lemon aroma.
effects: Drinking the concentrate straight is a sugar-and-acid shock: overwhelmingly sweet at first, then a sharp citrus burn that clings to the throat.
It feels syrupy and heavy, leaving a sticky, mouth-coating residue that demands water afterward.

name: Savory Vegetable Broth (Canned)
descriptions: Clear, savory broth made from simmered vegetables and seasonings; warm and comforting.
Lightly salty with an umami backbone, good as a sipping broth or base for soups.
effects: You sip the warm broth — the salty, savory flavors feel soothing and easy to swallow, like a gentle comfort.
It settles quietly in your stomach and leaves a pleasant warmth spreading inward.

name: Aloe Vera Juice
descriptions: Slightly viscous, pale liquid marketed for soothing and digestive comfort; mildly bitter and herbal.
Often blended with light sweeteners to cut the medicinal notes.
effects: You swallow the thick aloe juice and notice a cooling, slightly medicinal flavor that slides down your throat.
It leaves a subtle aftertaste and a faintly calming sensation in the throat.

name: Berry Nectar (Strawberry & Blueberry, Sweetened)
descriptions: Processed berry nectar made from pressed berries and added sweeteners; smooth and intensely fruity.
Thicker than pure juice, with a bright berry perfume and pronounced sweetness.
effects: You drink the berry nectar and are met with a bold, candy-like berry sweetness; it's lush and immediately satisfying.
The texture is slightly syrupy, making it feel indulgent with each swallow.

name: Carrot-Ginger Shot
descriptions: A small concentrated shot of carrot juice with a sharp ginger kick; spicy and bright.
Served chilled in a small vial, meant for a quick, potent boost.
effects: You down the carrot-ginger shot in one go — the vegetable sweetness is immediately followed by a hot, spicy ginger bite that warms the sinuses.
It leaves a tingling heat in your throat and a cleansing, brisk sensation overall.
